title: Officer cleared in fatal shooting: Sudanese community 'disappointed'
article: A Crown prosecutor in Edmonton has cleared a Calgary police officer of any wrongdoing in the fatal shooting of a Sudanese man who attacked him with a knife.
The decision disappointed Calgary's Sudanese community.
A review of the case by the province's special prosecutions branch released Thursday said Const. Ira Macumber acted in self- defence when he shot Deng Fermino Kuol, 34, on Oct. 25, 2003.
"It's very, very unfortunate a death had to occur, but our officer is protected by law in using force when his life is in jeopardy," Calgary police Chief Jack Beaton said.
"The report found our officer acted reasonably and justifiably."
The finding is little comfort to some members of the city's Sudanese community, who accused police of using excessive force and called for an independent inquiry into the shooting.
"I'm extremely, extremely disappointed, but not surprised at the same time," said Martin Yak, chairman of the Sudanese Community Relations Committee.
"This case was closed before it was even opened."
Yak declined further comment, saying he would be meeting with Kuol's family and the committee to explore options.

The Calgary Police Service policy dictates that any shooting involving an officer be investigated by the homicide unit, with the findings then forwarded to the Crown and the service's professional standards section for review.
While the Crown's report ends any criminal investigation into the shooting, it will still be subject to a public fatality inquiry. No date has been set.
Reached at home Thursday, Macumber declined comment until after that inquiry has taken place.
The 40-year-old, four-year member of the police force returned to duty about two weeks after the shooting.
Macumber was alone when he responded to a disturbance call at 1709 37th St. S.E. shortly after midnight on Oct. 25.
Kuol was banging on the door of a basement suite shared by his uncle and a friend, loudly demanding to be let in. The friend, unwilling to let the intoxicated Kuol in, called police.
Investigators said after initially agreeing to go with Macumber, Kuol drew a knife and slashed the officer on the left arm.
The knife cut through several layers of clothing and caused a gash to Macumber's arm.
As Macumber and Kuol struggled over control of the knife, the officer was able to draw his gun with his free hand and fire twice.
The shots struck Kuol in the neck, and he died in hospital a short time later.
Firing two shots is in keeping with police training, under which officers are taught to aim at an aggressor's central body mass.
The head of the union representing Calgary's rank and file police officers said Macumber heeded his training and was justified in using deadly force to stop Kuol.
"It's unfortunate the tragedy had to occur. However, it was a life-and-death situation and decisions had to be made at the time," said Al Koenig.
Nevertheless, the outcome has been hard to accept for some who knew Kuol, who came to Canada in search of a better life five years ago.
Kuol was one of the so-called Lost Boys of Sudan, a legion of thousands of child and teenage refugees who fled Sudan's long- running civil war.
Many found refuge in Cuba, where Kuol went on to graduate from college as a veterinary technician.
Those qualifications meant little when Kuol arrived in Brooks, and he found work instead at the local meat packing plant.
He lost his job in the weeks before his death and he had become a heavy drinker -- a problem that resulted in several arrests by the RCMP.
Kuol was also accused of assaulting a city police officer who attempted to arrest him on June 2, at the same apartment where the fatal shooting took place.
While the Crown has cleared Macumber of any wrongdoing, Beaton said the police service will have to overcome lingering suspicion among some in the Calgary's 7,500-member Sudanese community.
"I do know they're upset about this shooting. . . . We will continue to work with that community," he said. "There is some healing that has to take place."
